Getting started

Before anything is decided

Nothing here commits you to anything. People ask questions at this parish for a long time before any decision is made, and some go on asking happily for years.

What is an inquirer?

Someone who is asking questions about the Orthodox Church. Nothing is being asked of you in return.

An inquirer is simply someone who is looking into the Orthodox faith — coming to services, reading, asking questions, and seeing what the life of the Church is like from the inside.

No commitment is implied. Inquirers' conversations happen quietly and at your own pace, often over many months. You are welcome to keep coming, keep reading, and take as long as you need.

What is a catechumen?

Someone the Church has formally set on the path towards being received, and who is being taught along the way.

A catechumen is someone who has moved from looking on to preparing: the Church has received them as a learner, prays for them by name in her services, and teaches them in the time before their baptism or chrismation. The word is as old as the Church herself.

How a person becomes a catechumen here, and what that time looks like at the Nativity, is Fr. John's to describe rather than ours.

Do I need to be sure I want to become Orthodox before I start asking questions?

No. Questions come first, and they are welcome long before any decision is.

Speak with Fr. John — no commitment is implied by it. People ask questions here for a long time before anything is decided, and some never move beyond asking. Both are honourable.

You are welcome to keep coming, keep reading, and take as long as you need.

Who should I ask when I have questions?

Fr. John. The parish office will arrange a conversation.

Fr. John is the person to ask, and the parish office is the way to reach him: contact the office to arrange a conversation.

Parishioners are glad to answer what they can, and a good deal can be learned over coffee after the Liturgy. But an answer about your own situation should come from your priest rather than from the person standing next to you — or from a web page.

Contact the parish office →

What should I read?

Ask Fr. John what to read next. The parish bookstore keeps books written for inquirers and catechumens.

The reading that helps one person is not the reading that helps another, so the list that matters is the one Fr. John gives you.

The parish bookstore is open every Sunday after the Divine Liturgy and stocks books, prayer books and pamphlets, including shelves meant for inquirers and for those coming into the Church.
